rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.text:
People struggle with three kinds of old photos they only vaguely remember. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Among photos kept as memories (people, trips, events), 13 of 48 stories (27%) say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:sentimental]] Among photos whose post does not say why they were kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) say the same — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:unclear]] For photos kept for information (receipts, documents, notes), 8 of 21 stories say the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]] One person wrote they needed an “old screenshot picc.” [[story|313e52d4d7afb19798f4bb12be3491ecf5803425:0]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary by what first went wrong, across all kinds?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot reliably show what people remember, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]]

People often remember what was in the photo, like the main subject or people present. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=who:people_present@photo_class:_all]]  
Some remember when it was taken, such as the year. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:_all]]  
A few remember where it was taken or the event. [[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:where:core]][[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:event:core]]  
One person wrote they found it by searching “the words on the posters” — “threw them up immediately.” [[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary focused only on time, place, and people?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.text:
People most often forgot when the photo was taken. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] They also forgot the date or year. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]] Some forgot where it was taken, like the exact place or venue name. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]] A few forgot whether it was a photo, video, or screenshot, or which app or account it was in. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]] One post fits this: “Photos with no metadata, listed as JPEGS, under the wrong year.” [[story|eb1a88bd470868f13eabf5ce1386418e831b7917:0]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want me to group these by what people still remembered?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
withheld: label-and-colon opening: Many such searches work:
rows.draft:
People often type a simple word or object they remember, like bicycle, posters, or vomit. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]][[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]][[story|88a83897e2c872e72ac85967d7fc5c158d43bbb0:0]] Many such searches work: 38 of 115 stories (33%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered ended with the photo found. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]] But in 31 of 115 stories (27%), the search did not understand what they typed or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] One person wrote, “I just search Google Photos for ‘bicycle’, and find it.” [[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.text:
- In 38 of 115 stories (33%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]]
- In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: The stories cannot provide product financial figures for Google Photos — they contain only user stories about searching for photos and no financial or revenue data. These are public posts about trying to find a photo, so they cannot answer this question. To answer it, we would need audited financial statements or official company disclosures that break out Google Photos revenue.

Here is the split by kind of photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=1@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:sentimental]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:unclear]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:utility]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]]

Among photos kept as memories, 13 of 48 stories (27%) first went wrong when the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]  
In the same memories group, 6 of 48 stories (12%) first went wrong because the photo was already gone — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:sentimental]]  
Also in memories, 6 of 48 stories (12%) first went wrong when people never used the search box — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:sentimental]]  
One person said “Two faces” yielded nothing. [[story|3b53d4e5bf5f572ac92dce7bbc1051e9491c662a:0]]

Among photos whose post does not say why they were kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) first went wrong when the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]]  
In that same group, 6 of 46 stories (13%) first went wrong because the photo was already gone — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:unclear]]  
Also there, 6 of 46 stories (13%) first went wrong because the photo was in the results but hard to spot — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:unclear]]

Among photos kept for the information in them, 8 of 21 stories first went wrong because the photo was already gone. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]]  
In that same information group, 3 of 21 stories first went wrong when the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.text:
Most often, the search misunderstands what people type, or shows the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
Some say the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]  
At times, the photo is in the results but hard to spot among similar ones. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:_all]]  
One person wrote that “'dog park' never finds the photo of my dog at the park in winter.” [[story|probe-inj-06]]  
One limit is that these are public posts and not a success rate for all searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
